translation:
The target introduces two definitions:

1. `Def7`: Given an arithmetic theory `F` (a set of arithmetic sentences) together with the hypothesis that `F` is recursively enumerable (`F.RE`), `Def7 F` is defined (noncomputably) as the arithmetic sentence `F.craig.consistent.val`—that is, the sentence `¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝)`, where `F.craig` is the Δ₁-presented axiom set obtained from `F` by Craig's trick (having the same theorems as `F`), and `Prov_{F.craig}` is the standard provability predicate built from that Δ₁ presentation. No further assumptions on `F` (such as consistency, soundness, extending `𝗜𝚺₁`, or having a Δ₁ presentation of its own) are required.

2. `Def8`: Given a set of arithmetic sentences `K` (`Def1`), an arithmetic theory `F`, and the hypothesis that `F` is recursively enumerable (`F.RE`), `Def8 K F` is the proposition asserting that both of the following hold: (a) `Def5 K F`, meaning `K` is equal to `F.theory` (the set of all arithmetic sentences derivable from `F` in classical first-order logic), and (b) `Def7 F ∈ K`, meaning the consistency sentence `F.craig.consistent.val` is an element of `K`. Here `F` is an explicit parameter rather than a quantified variable, and no consistency, soundness, or strength hypotheses are placed on `K` or `F`.

divergences.description: Def8 completely omits the epistemic clause of knowing the exact specification of the machine one is—K(K = F_e) (SSMT) in P-K359 and P-K357—which plain first-order arithmetic (ℒₒᵣ) cannot express because it lacks an epistemic operator K in the object language. Instead, Def8 uses Def5 K F, i.e., the unmodalized extensional equality K = F.theory (WMT), which in P-K359 is the unexcluded background scenario rather than the excluded self-knowledge clause.

Def8 replaces knowing that the machine works correctly—glossed in P-K359 as soundness, K(F_e ⊆ T)—with knowing mere consistency, Def7 F ∈ K (i.e., Con(F.craig) ∈ K). Plain arithmetic cannot express F_e ⊆ T as a single sentence due to the lack of a truth predicate T, and consistency is materially weaker than soundness (a consistent formal system can still prove false arithmetic sentences), even though ruling out consistency yields a stronger negation than ruling out soundness.

Both Def7 and Def8 represent a formal system or theorem-proving computer by an extensional set of arithmetic axioms F with a proof-irrelevant r.e. witness [F.RE], and Def7 noncomputably applies Craig's trick (F.craig) to choose some Δ₁ presentation rather than using a canonical presentation of F (P-K345) or a specific Turing machine specification/index e as in F_e (P-K357, P-K359). In addition, Def5 K F identifies the computer's output with the classical first-order deductive closure F.theory.

Def7 and Def8 restrict both F and K to sentences of first-order arithmetic (ℒₒᵣ), whereas P-K345 emphasizes that Gödel's theorems apply to any sufficiently strong formal system and P-K359 speaks generally of mathematical intuition and theorem-proving computers.
Def8 leaves F as an explicit free parameter rather than existentially quantifying over a machine as in P-K357 and P-K359 (e.g., ∃e), requiring quantification to be supplied externally in theorems.

judgement.summary: While Def7 is a reasonable arithmetic formalization of Con(F) up to the restriction to ℒₒᵣ and the noncomputable use of Craig's trick, Def8 diverges materially from P-K359 and P-K357. Because plain arithmetic lacks both an epistemic operator K and a truth predicate T, Def8 drops K(K = F_e) (knowing one's own machine specification) in favor of mere extensional equality K = F.theory, and weakens K(F_e ⊆ T) (knowing the machine is sound) to Con(F.craig) ∈ K (knowing it is consistent).
